body:
: The operator picks a station and sees its parked robots.

* Shows each parked robot's id, status (READY, CHARGING, MAINTENANCE) and battery level
* Sorted by highest battery first, using a custom Comparator; equal battery ordered by robot id
* Clear messages for an unknown station and for a station with no robots
* Available as an option in the Planning App menu, with the operator role visible
* Unit tests.
title: USEI02 List the robots parked at a selected station

body:
The operator sees the capacity and occupation of all stations.

* Each station shows its id, name, maximum capacity, occupied spots and free spots
* Only READY, CHARGING and MAINTENANCE robots occupy a spot; BUSY robots are out delivering
* The data comes from the imported files (USEI01)
* Unit tests, including the large datasetgh sortParked).
title: USEI02 Station status service

body:
Order Queue Management and Time-Window Filtering
As a logistics operator, I want to manage and filter the queue of pending 
purchase orders by delivery time windows and customer ID, while keeping orders 
prioritized by their deadline.
o Acceptance Criteria:
– An ordered queue structure that automatically keeps pending 
orders sorted by their earliest delivery deadline.
– Filtered lists of orders matching specific criteria (e.g., orders due 
within the next hour or orders belonging to a specific customer ID).
– Functions to query and remove processed orders from the queue 
safely without breaking collection integrity.

title: USPL06

body:
Complex Order Partitioning Across Multiple Robots
As a logistics operator, I want to split oversized or incompatible purchase orders 
into sub-orders so that they can be dispatched across multiple robots when a 
single robot cannot fulfill the request.
o Acceptance Criteria:
– Algorithmically partitioned sub-orders where items are grouped 
legally by compatibility (e.g., separating refrigerated items from 
non-refrigerated items if required) and weight/volume constraints.
– Successful multi-robot assignment linking each sub-order to a 
distinct available robot.
– A structured summary showing the original order, the generated 
sub-orders, and their respective assigned robots.
title: USEI05

body:
Parking Station Monitoring and Control Console
User Story Objective: As a shopping facility operator, I want to consult the status 
of parking stations to monitor their total and available capacity, as well as the 
robots currently parked, including their status and battery levels sorted in 
descending order.
o Acceptance Criteria:
– A clear status view per station detailing maximum capacity, 
occupied spots, and free spots.
– A list of parked robots for a selected station showing their 
operational status (READY, CHARGING, MAINTENANCE) and 
battery levels.
– Sorted robot outputs driven by custom Comparator 
implementation (e.g., highest battery level first)
title: USEI02

body:
Data Import and System Initialization
As an infrastructure planner, I want to import initial information from text/CSV 
files (robots, parking stations, and user purchase requests) and load it into the 
most appropriate data structures.
o Acceptance Criteria:
– Successful parsing and loading of all entities (Robots, Stations, 
Orders) into Java Collection Framework structures without data 
loss or corruption.
– Appropriate collection choices based on access patterns.
– Informative error messages or logs for malformed lines or missing 
values during the import process.

body:
Feasibility Check and Single-Robot Assignment
As a logistics operator, I want to evaluate if a single purchase order can be
fulfilled by an available robot and assign the most suitable robot based on
weight, volume constraints, and highest battery level.
o Acceptance Criteria:
– A boolean feasibility result indicating whether any available robot
satisfies all constraints (max volume, max weight, and minimum
required battery).
– Automatic assignment of the order to the optimal robot (READY
status, sufficient capacity, and highest current battery).
– Updated status of the selected robot (e.g., state changed from
READY to BUSY) and updated station availability.
